points.description: Data members can be accessed by any member function of the class (class-wide scope), whereas local variables can only be accessed inside the single member function that defines them (function-only scope).
points.partial_credit: Half marks if only one side is stated (e.g. only that local variables are limited to their function), or the scope contrast is stated vaguely or with a minor error.

points.description: Explicitly contrasts the two: data members are shared across/accessible to all member functions in the class, while a local variable is not accessible to other member functions.
points.partial_credit: Half mark if the contrast is only implied.

rubric.notes: Full marks for stating that data members are accessible from all member functions of the class while local variables are only accessible inside the member function that declares them, in any wording. Give part marks if only one side is given or the scope idea is vague. Give no marks for answers that only talk about declaration location or type without any accessibility/scope contrast.
